questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A pressure group hires professionals to meet legislators privately and persuade them to support a bill. This method is
questions.A: lobbying
questions.B: a strike
questions.C: a boycott
questions.D: a demonstration
questions.explanation: Lobbying is the direct persuasion of decision-makers, named after the lobbies of parliament buildings.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of pressure groups to a democracy?
questions.A: they provide government with expert information and represent interests between elections
questions.B: they replace political parties in forming governments
questions.C: they conduct elections on behalf of the electoral commission
questions.D: they make laws for the country
questions.explanation: Pressure groups give citizens a continuous voice and supply specialised knowledge to policy-makers.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A criticism of pressure groups is that
questions.A: wealthy and well-organised groups may gain influence out of proportion to their numbers
questions.B: they never succeed in influencing government decisions no matter how well organised they are
questions.C: they are all controlled and financed by the government and merely echo its policies
questions.D: they must contest and win elections before the government will listen to their demands
questions.explanation: Rich groups can afford lobbyists and publicity that poorer groups cannot, distorting policy in their favour.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Bar Association is best classified as
questions.A: a professional pressure group
questions.B: a political party
questions.C: an anomic group
questions.D: a religious group
questions.explanation: Professional associations defend the interests and standards of their members.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Christian Association of Nigeria and the Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, when they seek to influence government policy, act as
questions.A: religious pressure groups
questions.B: political parties
questions.C: occupational groups
questions.D: anomic groups
questions.explanation: Religious bodies become pressure groups when they lobby government on matters affecting their faith.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A trade union calls its members out on strike to force an employer to raise wages. This method of pressure is
questions.A: industrial action
questions.B: lobbying
questions.C: litigation
questions.D: propaganda
questions.explanation: Strikes withdraw labour to impose costs on employers or government until demands are met.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A human rights group goes to court to challenge a law it considers oppressive. This method is
questions.A: litigation
questions.B: lobbying
questions.C: a boycott
questions.D: a strike
questions.explanation: Groups use the courts to test the legality of government actions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The success of a pressure group depends largely on
questions.A: its size, finances, organisation and access to decision-makers
questions.B: the number of candidates it fields in elections
questions.C: the number of ministries it controls
questions.D: its ability to conduct elections
questions.explanation: Well-funded, well-led groups with close links to government are most effective.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigeria Union of Journalists differs from a political party in that it
questions.A: seeks to influence policies affecting its members without contesting elections
questions.B: sponsors candidates for the National Assembly and campaigns for them at elections
questions.C: forms the government and appoints ministers whenever it wins a general election
questions.D: is registered by the Independent National Electoral Commission before it can operate
questions.explanation: Pressure groups influence power from outside; parties seek to hold power.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public opinion is best described as
questions.A: the views of a large section of the public on an issue of general concern
questions.B: the private opinion of the head of state on matters affecting the government
questions.C: the official policy of the ruling party as stated in its election manifesto
questions.D: the decisions of the Supreme Court on questions of constitutional importance
questions.explanation: It is the collective attitude of the people on matters of public interest.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Newspapers, radio, television and social media help to form public opinion by
questions.A: providing information and a platform for debate on public issues
questions.B: conducting elections and announcing the results on behalf of the government
questions.C: making laws on behalf of the legislature when it is not in session
questions.D: appointing ministers and judges and supervising the work they do
questions.explanation: The mass media inform citizens and shape the way issues are discussed.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A government that ignores strong public opinion against a policy risks
questions.A: losing legitimacy and support at the next election
questions.B: increasing its popularity among the voters who opposed the policy
questions.C: being praised by the opposition parties for its firmness and courage
questions.D: having its policy adopted faster by the legislature and the courts
questions.explanation: In a democracy, persistent disregard of public feeling is punished at the polls or through protests.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public opinion polls are a useful guide to government because they
questions.A: measure the views of a sample of the population on specific issues
questions.B: replace the need for elections and other forms of popular participation
questions.C: always give completely accurate results that can never be questioned
questions.D: are conducted only by political parties and reflect the views of their members
questions.explanation: Scientific sampling allows the views of millions to be estimated from a few thousand respondents.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A limitation of public opinion as a guide to government is that
questions.A: it can be manipulated by propaganda and may be poorly informed
questions.B: it never changes over time
questions.C: it is always unanimous on every issue
questions.D: it can only be expressed through elections
questions.explanation: Opinion can be swayed by biased media or emotional appeals and may not reflect careful judgment.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A vote by the whole electorate on whether to accept a proposed policy is a direct way of measuring public opinion called
questions.A: a referendum
questions.B: an opinion poll
questions.C: a by-election
questions.D: a recall
questions.explanation: Referendums put a specific question directly to the people.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public opinion is difficult to determine precisely in Nigeria partly because of
questions.A: the diversity of languages, cultures and regions
questions.B: the small size of the population
questions.C: the absence of any mass media
questions.D: the existence of a one-party state
questions.explanation: Different sections of a diverse society often hold sharply different views, and many voices go unheard.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The #EndSARS protests of 2020 in Nigeria demonstrated that
questions.A: social media can mobilise public opinion rapidly against government policy
questions.B: public opinion has no effect whatsoever on the decisions of the government
questions.C: only registered political parties are able to organise nationwide protests
questions.D: the print press is the only effective channel for expressing public opinion
questions.explanation: Young Nigerians used social media to organise nationwide protests that led to the disbandment of the SARS police unit.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a channel for expressing public opinion?
questions.A: the secret deliberations of the cabinet
questions.B: letters to newspaper editors
questions.C: peaceful demonstrations
questions.D: radio phone-in programmes
questions.explanation: Cabinet deliberations are the government's own private discussions, not an expression of the public's views.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Freedom of the press is important for public opinion because it
questions.A: allows citizens to receive information and views free from government control
questions.B: guarantees that newspapers always support the government
questions.C: prevents citizens from criticising the government
questions.D: makes the press an arm of government
questions.explanation: Without a free press, citizens cannot form informed opinions or hear alternatives to official views.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The civil service is
questions.A: the body of permanent officials who implement government policies in the ministries
questions.B: the body of elected members who make laws in the legislature for a fixed term
questions.C: the body of commissioned officers who command the armed forces of the country
questions.D: the body of judges who interpret the law and administer justice in the superior courts
questions.explanation: Civil servants are career officials employed by the state to run its administration.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The political head of a federal ministry in Nigeria is the
questions.A: minister
questions.B: permanent secretary
questions.C: director-general
questions.D: head of service
questions.explanation: The minister is appointed by the President and gives political direction; the permanent secretary is the administrative head.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The recruitment, promotion and discipline of federal civil servants is the responsibility of the
questions.A: Federal Civil Service Commission
questions.B: National Assembly
questions.C: Independent National Electoral Commission
questions.D: Council of State
questions.explanation: The Civil Service Commission is an independent body that protects the service from political patronage.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Civil servants are expected to serve any government in power with equal loyalty. This is the principle of
questions.A: political neutrality (impartiality)
questions.B: anonymity
questions.C: permanence
questions.D: collective responsibility
questions.explanation: Neutrality allows the service to continue smoothly when governments change.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The principle of anonymity in the civil service means that civil servants
questions.A: are not publicly named or blamed for the advice they give ministers
questions.B: must work without being paid
questions.C: cannot be promoted
questions.D: must keep their identity secret from colleagues
questions.explanation: Ministers take public responsibility, so officials can advise frankly without fear.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The class of the civil service responsible for policy advice and top management of ministries is the
questions.A: administrative class
questions.B: clerical class
questions.C: executive class
questions.D: messengerial class
questions.explanation: Permanent secretaries and directors belong to the administrative class.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem of the Nigerian civil service?
questions.A: red tape and delays in decision-making
questions.B: excessive speed in implementing policies
questions.C: too few officials for the work
questions.D: the absence of any rules and procedures
questions.explanation: Excessive procedures and hierarchy slow down administration; corruption and poor pay are other problems.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Udoji Commission of 1974 is remembered mainly for
questions.A: reviewing salaries and structure of the public service
questions.B: creating the twelve-state structure
questions.C: drafting the 1979 Constitution
questions.D: establishing local government councils
questions.explanation: The Udoji awards greatly increased public service salaries and introduced a unified grading system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The principle of federal character in civil service appointments is meant to
questions.A: ensure that all states and groups are fairly represented in federal institutions
questions.B: reserve the top posts in federal institutions for candidates from the most populous states
questions.C: abolish merit completely as a basis for recruitment and promotion in the federal service
questions.D: limit recruitment into the federal service to university graduates from federal universities
questions.explanation: Section 14(3) of the 1999 Constitution requires that no section dominates federal appointments.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A civil servant differs from a public servant in a parastatal in that the civil servant
questions.A: works directly in a government ministry or department
questions.B: is not paid from public funds
questions.C: is elected by the people
questions.D: cannot be transferred from one post to another
questions.explanation: The public service is wider and includes staff of corporations, the police and the armed forces.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The civil service advises ministers on policy mainly because civil servants
questions.A: have specialised knowledge and long experience of government business
questions.B: are elected by the people and therefore represent the views of the electorate
questions.C: belong to the ruling party and are committed to carrying out its manifesto
questions.D: control the legislature and can ensure that the minister's bills are passed
questions.explanation: Ministers come and go, but career officials accumulate expertise in their fields.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following would improve the efficiency of the Nigerian civil service?
questions.A: merit-based recruitment, regular training and adequate pay
questions.B: appointing only the relatives and friends of ministers to senior posts
questions.C: abolishing all rules of procedure so that officials can act as they wish
questions.D: removing security of tenure so that officials can be dismissed at any time
questions.explanation: Competent, well-trained and well-paid staff are less prone to corruption and more productive.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The most senior career civil servant in Nigeria's federal service is the
questions.A: Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
questions.B: Secretary to the Government of the Federation
questions.C: Minister of Finance
questions.D: Chief of Staff to the President
questions.explanation: The Head of Service coordinates the ministries and represents the career service.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A public corporation is
questions.A: a business enterprise owned and controlled by the government and set up by law
questions.B: a business enterprise owned by private shareholders and registered under company law
questions.C: a government ministry headed by a minister and staffed by career civil servants
questions.D: a local government council elected by the people of a local government area
questions.explanation: Examples include the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Nigerian Television Authority.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of a public corporation?
questions.A: it is established by an Act of parliament and is a separate legal entity
questions.B: it is owned by private shareholders who elect its board of directors at annual meetings
questions.C: its profits are shared among its workers at the end of every financial year
questions.D: it is exempt from all forms of ministerial, legislative and judicial control
questions.explanation: Corporations can sue and be sued in their own names and are run by boards appointed by government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public corporations are usually set up to provide services such as electricity and water because
questions.A: the huge capital required and the need to serve all citizens make private provision unattractive
questions.B: private firms are forbidden by the constitution to engage in any form of business activity
questions.C: public corporations are always more efficient and better managed than private companies
questions.D: the government wants to make large profits from these services to finance its budget
questions.explanation: Essential services with heavy capital needs and low returns are often left to the state.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A common problem of public corporations in Nigeria is
questions.A: political interference in appointments and management
questions.B: excessive profits that cannot be spent
questions.C: a shortage of government funds for salaries only
questions.D: the absence of a board of directors
questions.explanation: Politicians often use corporations for patronage, appointing unqualified officials and directing contracts.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Public corporations are controlled by the legislature through
questions.A: the examination of their accounts and annual reports by committees
questions.B: the appointment of their general managers and other senior officers
questions.C: the daily supervision of their operations by members of the legislature
questions.D: the fixing of the prices they charge for their goods and services
questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee scrutinises the reports of the Auditor-General on corporations.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Ministerial control of a public corporation is exercised mainly through
questions.A: the power to appoint the board and issue policy directives
questions.B: the sale of the corporation's shares to members of the public
questions.C: court cases brought against the corporation by the minister
questions.D: the daily running of its offices by officials of the ministry
questions.explanation: The supervising minister sets broad policy but is not supposed to interfere in day-to-day management.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Under the Petroleum Industry Act, the NNPC was converted into NNPC Limited, a company registered under the Companies and Allied Matters Act. This is an example of
questions.A: commercialisation
questions.B: nationalisation
questions.C: confiscation
questions.D: indigenisation
questions.explanation: Commercialisation requires a public enterprise to operate profitably like a private company while the state retains ownership.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Privatisation differs from commercialisation in that privatisation
questions.A: transfers ownership of the enterprise to private investors
questions.B: keeps the enterprise fully owned by the government
questions.C: involves the state taking over a private firm
questions.D: means the enterprise must provide free services
questions.explanation: Under commercialisation the state keeps ownership but demands profitability.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The agency responsible for implementing the privatisation of public enterprises in Nigeria is the
questions.A: Bureau of Public Enterprises
questions.B: Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.C: Federal Civil Service Commission
questions.D: Code of Conduct Bureau
questions.explanation: The BPE was created under the Public Enterprises (Privatisation and Commercialisation) Act of 1999.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: An argument in favour of privatisation is that it
questions.A: improves efficiency by exposing enterprises to competition and the profit motive
questions.B: guarantees lower prices for all consumers regardless of the cost of production
questions.C: increases the number of government employees and the size of the public service
questions.D: removes the need for any government regulation of the privatised enterprises
questions.explanation: Private owners have stronger incentives to cut waste and satisfy customers.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: An argument against privatisation in Nigeria is that
questions.A: national assets may be sold cheaply to a few wealthy individuals and foreign firms
questions.B: it always increases government control over the enterprises that are sold
questions.C: it leads to the employment of far more workers than the enterprises can afford
questions.D: it makes public services free of charge and therefore too costly for the state
questions.explanation: Critics point to under-valued sales, job losses and the concentration of ownership.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Auditor-General of the Federation contributes to the control of public corporations by
questions.A: auditing their accounts and reporting to the National Assembly
questions.B: appointing their chief executives and members of their boards
questions.C: fixing the prices of the goods and services that they provide
questions.D: approving their annual budgets before they are sent to the minister
questions.explanation: Independent audit exposes waste and fraud for legislative scrutiny.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Local government is described as the third tier of government in Nigeria because it
questions.A: is the level of government closest to the people, below the federal and state governments
questions.B: was the first level of government to be created before the federal and state governments
questions.C: controls the other two levels of government and supervises the way they spend money
questions.D: has the largest budget of the three levels and employs the greatest number of workers
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms and the constitution recognise local government as a distinct tier with its own functions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a function of local governments under the Fourth Schedule of the 1999 Constitution?
questions.A: establishment and maintenance of markets, motor parks and cemeteries
questions.B: printing of the national currency and control of the money supply
questions.C: conduct of foreign relations and signing of treaties with other countries
questions.D: control of the armed forces and defence of the country against attack
questions.explanation: Local councils also register births and deaths, name streets, collect rates and provide refuse disposal.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major source of internally generated revenue for a local government is
questions.A: tenement rates and market fees
questions.B: customs duties on imports
questions.C: company income tax
questions.D: petroleum profits tax
questions.explanation: Rates, licences, fees and fines are collected locally; the biggest source of council income remains the statutory allocation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The largest source of revenue for most local governments in Nigeria is
questions.A: statutory allocation from the Federation Account
questions.B: tenement rates collected from property owners
questions.C: fees collected from traders in council markets
questions.D: fines imposed by customary and area courts
questions.explanation: Most councils depend heavily on their share of federally collected revenue.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A reason for creating local governments is to
questions.A: bring government nearer to the people and encourage grassroots participation
questions.B: reduce the number of civil servants employed by the federal and state governments
questions.C: take over all the functions of the state governments in the rural areas of the country
questions.D: abolish traditional institutions and replace chiefs with elected council officials
questions.explanation: Local councils handle local problems that distant central governments cannot manage well.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The chief executive of a local government council in Nigeria is the
questions.A: chairman
questions.B: governor
questions.C: secretary
questions.D: councillor
questions.explanation: The elected chairman heads the executive arm; councillors form the legislative arm.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The joint state-local government account in Nigeria has been criticised because
questions.A: state governments often withhold or divert funds meant for local councils
questions.B: local governments receive too much money through it
questions.C: it is controlled by the federal government
questions.D: it prevents states from receiving any allocation
questions.explanation: Funds pass through the states, which sometimes deduct or delay them, weakening council autonomy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Local government administration in Nigeria is often weakened by
questions.A: the dissolution of elected councils by state governors and the appointment of caretaker committees
questions.B: the excessive independence of the councils from both the state and the federal governments
questions.C: the holding of too many elections at the local level, which leaves no time for development work
questions.D: the refusal of the councils to accept statutory allocations from the Federation Account
questions.explanation: Caretaker committees appointed by governors undermine the democratic character of local government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Supreme Court judgment of July 2024 on local government autonomy held that
questions.A: allocations from the Federation Account should be paid directly to democratically elected local councils
questions.B: local governments should be abolished and their functions transferred to the state governments
questions.C: state governors may lawfully dissolve elected councils and appoint chairmen of their choice
questions.D: local councils need not hold elections as long as the state House of Assembly approves
questions.explanation: The court ruled that states must not retain local government funds and that only elected councils should receive them.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: State Independent Electoral Commissions are responsible for
questions.A: conducting local government elections
questions.B: conducting governorship elections
questions.C: registering political parties
questions.D: conducting presidential elections
questions.explanation: SIECs are established by Section 197 of the 1999 Constitution to organise council elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Traditional rulers in Nigeria today mainly play a role in local administration by
questions.A: advising on customs and helping to maintain peace and order
questions.B: making by-laws for the councils and approving their annual budgets
questions.C: collecting federal taxes such as company income tax and customs duties
questions.D: commanding the local police and presiding over the magistrates' courts
questions.explanation: They serve on advisory councils and act as links between government and the people.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a problem facing local governments in Nigeria?
questions.A: shortage of qualified staff and inadequate finance
questions.B: excessive autonomy from the states
questions.C: too much revenue from internal sources
questions.D: lack of any functions to perform
questions.explanation: Poor funding, low-skilled staff, corruption and interference combine to limit council performance.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Local governments participate in primary education mainly by
questions.A: helping to provide and maintain primary schools
questions.B: awarding university degrees
questions.C: setting national examinations
questions.D: training secondary school teachers
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule gives councils a role in the provision and maintenance of primary, adult and vocational education.
